title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-scratchpad
content:
Context:
I started a quick investigation after customer report + internal alert: overall token throughput dropped ~20-40% for chat workloads on dedicated clusters (p1000-prod-1). Suspected continuous batching behavior changed after the last runtime deploy (v1.24.0).

What I observed (summary):
- Baseline (pre-regression): 450k tokens/min for 8xA100 pool, avg downstream latency 110ms/token under steady load of mixed seq-len 64/256.
- Current: ~300k tokens/min under same load profile, latency higher and CPU on the batcher process spikes intermittently.
- GPU utilization is similar (~60-70%) but TPU (?) no, GPUs. Bottleneck appears earlier in CPU batching stage (batch assembly, KV cache checks).

Commands I ran (quick log):
- k8s logs
  kubectl -n infra logs deploy/serving-runtime-batcher-0 --since=2h | grep -i "batch"
  -> lots of 'small-batch flush' entries, more frequent than before.
- metrics snapshot
  kubectl exec -it deploy/serving-runtime-batcher-0 -- curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | egrep "batch_size|batch_flush|kvcache_hit"
  -> batch_size_p95 1.8 (used to be ~4.7), batch_flush_count increased by ~3x in the regression window.
- load test (local)
  python tools/load_test.py --host https://dedicated-prod.rw --model redwood-1 --qps 600 --seq_len_dist "[0.6:64,0.4:256]" --duration 10m
  -> generated stable qps, observed throughput drop and high tail latency ~1.8s for some requests.
- perf traces
  curl -s http://localhost:8080/debug/trace | jq .samples | head -n50
  -> samples show time spent in BatchAssembler::assemble(), and KVCache::lookup dominates CPU.

Error / log snippets (copied):
- "[WARN] batcher: small-batch flush triggered (age_ms=12, count=1)"
- "[INFO] kvcache: miss route=prefix/conv-id id=..." (miss ratio jumped after config change)
- "[ERROR] batcher: flush rejected due to concurrency slot exhaustion" (rare but present)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Config change in v1.24.0 reduced the max batching window (ms) or increased "eager flush" threshold -> smaller batch sizes and more flushes -> lower throughput.
2) KV cache behavior changed (TTL or sharding) increasing miss rate -> more CPU per-request doing KV lookups -> batch assembly slower.
3) Scheduling change: batcher threads count reduced or thread affinity changed causing lock contention.
4) Network-level latencies increased (unlikely; GPU util steady).
5) Load shape subtle difference (more bursty small requests) — but internal load generator reproduces the issue, so config/runtime likely root cause.

Config files & diffs I checked:
- rollout manifest: infra/helm/serving-runtime/values.yaml (checked last two releases). Noted these diffs:
  - batching.window_ms: 16 -> 8 (this would explain more frequent flushes)
  - batching.max_batch_size: 64 -> 128 (confusing with lower window_ms but maybe combined with eager_flush true)
  - batching.eager_flush: false -> true

Quick experiments I ran (results):
- Reverted batching.window_ms to 16 locally (on staging cluster) and re-ran load_test: batch_size_p95 returned to ~4.6, throughput recovered ~+25% vs regression, tail latency improved.
- Turned off eager_flush: similar improvement.
- Reconfigured KV cache TTL to longer and increased cache shards from 8->16: marginal improvement in CPU time per request (~6% better), not enough by itself.

Intermediate conclusion:
- The primary regression is the combination of window_ms reduction + eager_flush=true in v1.24.0. That makes the batch assembler flush much more aggressively, causing smaller batches despite an increase in max_batch_size. Smaller batches push more per-request overhead and increase CPU work (KV lookups per micro-batch), reducing overall token throughput. KV cache mis-tuning is a secondary amplifier.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why was eager_flush turned on? Is there a latency SLO that motivated this (low-latency for single-shot requests) and did we unintentionally make it global? Need to check PR notes.
- Are any customers actually using the feature intentionally? Need to check feature flags per-customer.
- Does canary rollout accidentally target dedicated clusters (wrong overlay)?

Next immediate steps (action items):
- Revert eager_flush -> false and window_ms -> 16 in prod for the affected dedicated pools as an emergency mitigation (low-risk config change). (Assign: Miguel)
- Add a unit/integration test that asserts batch_size_p95 stays above X under synthetic workload to prevent future regressions. (Assign: Leah)
- Add telemetry event for 'eager_flush enabled' including scope (global / pool / customer) + rollup in console. (Assign: me)
- Create postmortem stub and link to ENG-4123 (I'll fill timeline + decision rationale).

Notes to self:
- When making change, watch for downstream latency SLO regressions for very low-QPS single-shot requests. Might need to add per-route overrides instead of global eager_flush.
- Consider smarter policy: eager_flush=true only when expected seq_len < 64 or when latency SLO tight; else rely on window_ms heuristics.

Useful commands / snippets to rerun quickly: 
- check batch metrics (prod):
  kubectl -n prod logs deploy/serving-runtime-batcher-0 --tail=200 | egrep "batch_size|small-batch flush|eager_flush"
- run local load test: 
  python tools/load_test.py --host https://dedicated-prod.rw --model redwood-1 --qps 600 --seq_len_dist "[0.6:64,0.4:256]" --duration 10m --report perf_report.json
- flip config (helm):
  helm upgrade --reuse-values serving-runtime infra/helm/serving-runtime -f patches/disable-eager-flush.yaml --namespace prod

Perf numbers to track in the postmortem: 
- token throughput (tokens/min) baseline vs current vs after mitigation
- batch_size_p50/p95
- kvcache hit ratio
- CPU time in BatchAssembler and KVCache fns
- tail latency (p95/p99) for chat route

Longer-term ideas:
- Add adaptive batching that tunes window_ms based on observed request interarrival times and sequence lengths per-route.
- Expose per-customer overrides and guard rails (e.g., "eager_flush allowed only for routes < 50ms target").
- Improve telemetry: record why a flush happened (max_size / window_expired / eager_flush / forced).

Links & references:
- PR that introduced changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/876
- Jira: ENG-4123 (throughput regression dedicated clusters)
- Slack: #serving-runtime thread: https://slack.com/archives/C12345/p1612345678000

Other breadcrumbs: 
- Rollout history: deploy/v1.24.0 -> v1.24.1 (hotfix reverted some unrelated logging). Need to confirm if v1.24.0 was rolled to dedicated or only to a subset.
- Customer report: "We see 30% higher billing for same workload due to more tokens/timeouts" (CS ticket 9982).

Status: mitigation tested in staging, ready for emergency config flip in prod once Miguel gives thumbs-up. Postmortem + tests on my todo for next week.

----
Scratch area (raw commands I ran and pasted):
$ kubectl -n prod exec -it svc/serving-runtime-batcher-0 -- curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | egrep "batch_size|batch_flush"
batcher_batch_size_p95 1.8
batcher_flush_count_total 34812
kvcache_hit_ratio 0.62

$ python tools/load_test.py --host https://dedicated-prod.rw --model redwood-1 --qps 600 --seq_len_dist "[0.6:64,0.4:256]" --duration 600
-- observed throughput: 305k tokens/min

$ helm get values serving-runtime -n prod > current-values.yaml
# patched to revert eager flush:
cat <<EOF > patches/disable-eager-flush.yaml
batching:
  window_ms: 16
  eager_flush: false
EOF

helm upgrade --reuse-values serving-runtime infra/helm/serving-runtime -f patches/disable-eager-flush.yaml --namespace prod

(Will monitor metrics for next 30m after flip)
